name: Monaco
summary_text: Monaco is workable for trans visitors — safe in practice, thin in law. Hate crimes and hate speech based on sexual orientation are penalised, and discrimination on grounds including gender identity is banned. There is no functioning legal gender recognition process (ILGA-Europe lists Monaco among states without one), but that is a resident-facing gap: a visitor faces no legal exposure whatsoever. Monaco is a tiny, heavily-policed, very low-crime tourist enclave embedded in France; street violence of any kind is rare. No bathroom laws, no border friction (entry via France, Schengen rules), no documented anti-trans incidents. The score reflects the gap between de facto safety (very high) and legal thinness (no LGR, limited explicit trans protections). Caveat: very small population — the evidence base is thin, so this assessment carries greater-than-usual uncertainty.

sources.title: Monaco | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex intimacy legal but very few protections - cohabitation agreements only (no marriage or adoption); hate crimes/speech on sexual orientation penalised; no SOGISC discrimination ban; no legal procedure for name/gender change, though in 2022 a trans person changed markers via an affirmative court decision for the first time; no nonbinary recognition; IGM not banned; no official Pride; limited visibility.

sources.title: Guide gay de Monaco et Destination gay de Monaco
sources.claim_summary: GayVoyageur (in French): gay travel guide for Monaco - LGBT-friendly accommodation and destination information for the principality.

US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Monaco: no significant changes; significant issues limited to libel and lèse-majesté laws (not enforced); no torture, arbitrary detention or other abuses reported.

Nice-Matin via Monaco's Haut Commissariat (March 2025, in French): 'Transmission, filiation, congé parental, nationalité... les personnes LGBT face aux défis du quotidien à Monaco' - homosexuality decriminalised since the 18th century, yet Monaco ranks near the bottom of European LGBT-rights rankings; no equal succession, survivor pensions or parental leave; only ~10 people dare be out; Council of Europe rapporteur Béatrice Fresko-Rolfo: 'C'est le triste bilan de Monaco'.
